walkthroughs.body_html:
v² = u² + 2 × a × s

u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, a = acceleration, s = distance.

This one's gold when you don't know the time. Just plug in what you've got.

Drop something. Ignoring air resistance, it accelerates at g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (often rounded to 10).

Drop a ball from rest. After 2 s, its speed is 0 + 9.8 × 2 ≈ 20 m/s. 🍏

In real life, air resistance kicks in and the object eventually hits terminal velocity.

Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance.

Thinking distance grows with speed and reaction time (tiredness, alcohol, phones 🚫).

Braking distance grows with speed squared. Wet roads, worn tyres, and heavy loads all make it worse.
